title: The frustration with UVA football is real, but the core problem is larger than any player, coach or single individual. I
title_zh:
弗吉尼亚大学足球队的挫败感是真实存在的，但核心问题比任何球员、教练或个人都更大。在我看来，这是一个商业问题。

夏洛茨维尔（我们的 Good Feet 商店之一就坐落于此）是美国最小的电视市场之一。如今的田径运动依赖于多年的品牌交易、NIL
full_text_en:
The frustration with UVA football is real, but the core problem is larger than any player, coach or single individual. In my view, it is a business problem.

Charlottesville (where one of our Good Feet stores resides) is one of the smallest TV markets in the country. Athletics today run on multi-year brand deals, NIL collectives, and revenue flywheels from large alumni bases and proximity to major corporate HQs. UVA lacks the geographical advantages and lacks the scale and reach of Ohio State, Michigan, Texas, or Florida. That is a structural constraint.

UVA’s football fan base is more fragile (not a fault of fans) due to a lack of a winning tradition compared to the power programs—Alabama, Texas, Oklahoma, Ohio State, Michigan, USC. Those are the Amazon, Walmarts and Coca-Colas of college football. They can operate on tradition and confidence that their customers will be back even when they miss. UVA cannot afford many misses and has to be scrappy: more creative, more personal, and more deliberate about every fan, donor, and sponsor. Otherwise the support of the fan base erodes quickly. The football program would make a strong Darden case study on building without the giants’ natural advantages.

In 2021 we were early NIL partners with UVA. We started with Kihei Clark on TV spots, then expanded to other athletes in UVA-logo jerseys, attaching millions in Good Feet advertising to the UVA brand. We followed the university’s approach: not pay-to-play, but real marketing leverage, inviting players to conferences, networking, and speaking opportunities. We did the same for others in football, men’s and women’s basketball, and non-rev sports. We are not a major Fortune 500 brand but we have made meaningful investments and will match our heart with anyone.

Two years ago major money flowed into UVA football. Problem solved, or so it seemed! Emphasis seemed to shift to seven and eight-figure checks. Those are wonderful gifts but that is not a sustainable model. Amazon, Coca-Cola, and Walmart, built flywheels one customer at a time.

Is it possible that those generous donations muddied good strategic thinking? It seems there is need of a strategy that attaches value at every level: the single fan with family at a few games, season-ticket holders and lower-level donors, small businesses attaching to the brand, larger sponsors, mid-tier five- and six-figure donors, and the premium seven-to-eight figure donors. When you are customer focused, you are accountable to those customers. Is it possible, that greater accountability to customers up and down the ladder, could foster better football strategy?

Tradition and humility can go together; tradition and entitlement cannot. Academic excellence and history are strengths, not automatic equalizers to the football powers. Be accountable to the people paying the bills, make hard, strategic decisions, be creative, listen. Embrace being David because you will never be Goliath. Winning will come.
full_text_zh:
弗吉尼亚大学足球队的挫败感是真实存在的，但核心问题比任何球员、教练或个人都更大。在我看来，这是一个商业问题。

夏洛茨维尔（我们的 Good Feet 商店之一就坐落于此）是美国最小的电视市场之一。如今的田径运动依赖于多年的品牌交易、NIL 集体以及来自大型校友基地和靠近主要公司总部的收入飞轮。 UVA 缺乏地理优势，也缺乏俄亥俄州、密歇根州、德克萨斯州或佛罗里达州的规模和覆盖范围。这是一个结构性限制。

与阿拉巴马州、德克萨斯州、俄克拉荷马州、俄亥俄州、密歇根州、南加州大学等实力项目相比，UVA 的橄榄球迷基础更加脆弱（不是球迷的错），因为缺乏获胜传统。这些是大学橄榄球界的亚马逊、沃尔玛和可口可乐。他们可以秉承传统经营，并相信即使顾客错过了，他们也会回来。 UVA 不能承受太多的失误，必须斗志昂扬：更有创意、更个性化、对每一位粉丝、捐助者和赞助商都更加深思熟虑。否则粉丝群的支持很快就会消失。足球项目将为达顿在没有巨人队天然优势的情况下进行建设提供强有力的案例研究。

2021 年，我们成为 UVA 的早期 NIL 合作伙伴。我们首先在电视广告中让基黑·克拉克 (Kihei Clark) 上场，然后扩展到穿着 UVA 徽标球衣的其他运动员，为 UVA 品牌投放了数百万美元的 Good Feet 广告。我们遵循了大学的方法：不是付费游戏，而是真正的营销杠杆，邀请玩家参加会议、社交和演讲机会。我们对足球、男子和女子篮球以及非职业体育运动中的其他人也做了同样的事情。我们不是财富 500 强的主要品牌，但我们进行了有意义的投资，并将与任何人心心相印。

两年前，大量资金流入弗吉尼亚大学橄榄球队。问题解决了，至少看起来是这样！重点似乎转向七位数和八位数的支票。这些都是很棒的礼物，但这不是一个可持续的模式。亚马逊、可口可乐和沃尔玛一次为一位客户制造飞轮。

这些慷慨的捐赠是否有可能混淆了良好的战略思维？似乎需要一种在各个层面赋予价值的策略：与家人一起观看几场比赛的单一球迷、季票持有者和较低级别的捐赠者、依附于品牌的小型企业、较大的赞助商、中型五位数和六位数的捐赠者以及高级七到八位数的捐赠者。当您以客户为中心时，您就要对这些客户负责。对上下级客户承担更大的责任是否有可能促进更好的足球战略？

传统与谦逊可以并存；传统和权利不能。卓越的学术成就和历史是优势，而不是足球强国的自动均衡器。对支付账单的人负责，做出艰难的战略决策，发挥创造力，倾听。拥抱成为大卫，因为你永远不会成为歌利亚。胜利将会到来。

author_role: President and CEO of Easy Step Enterprises, dba The Good Feet Store in VA, NC, MD,DC,OH. Love Jesus, my wife, our 5 kids, and 13 grandchildren. Go Hoos!

full_text_en:
LLMs accumulate a lot of declarative knowledge.
That's how they can answer a large number of questions. 
That's also why they require so many parameters and hence so much memory. 

But one can replace the accumulation of knowledge by *understanding*
That what JEPA world models do. 
That's one reason they can be useful with considerably less memory and training data  than LLMs. 

This paper merely shows that the underlying similarity structure of the data, whether text or image (e.g. co-occurence of words in text or objects in images) uniquely determines the shape of the representation point cloud, when the encoder is trained trained with a common anti-collapse criterion like SIGReg or VCReg (not by reconstruction).

这就是与法学硕士相比，它们可以在内存和训练数据少得多的情况下发挥作用的原因之一。

本文仅表明，当使用 SIGReg 或 VCReg（不是通过重建）等通用防崩溃标准对编码器进行训练时，无论是文本还是图像（例如文本中单词的共现或图像中对象的共现），数据的底层相似性结构唯一地确定了表示点云的形状。

andrej karpathy, co-founder of openai, pulled 16M views on one idea: stop using AI to write code, use it to build a second brain that remembers every article, pdf, transcript and conversation you ever fed it

you point claude code at a folder, drop anything into it, and claude reads it, cross-links it with everything already there, and writes it into a living wiki. your knowledge finally compounds instead of leaking out of your head every friday

the stack:

→ brew install obsidian, mkdir ~/vault, cd ~/vault
→ run claude in that folder and type "init a knowledge vault with CLAUDE.md as the rules, /raw for sources, /wiki for your pages"
→ drop any file into /raw (youtube transcript, meeting notes, 400-page pdf, screenshot of a tweet) and type "ingest"

5 minutes to set up. compounding knowledge from that evening forward

the ugly part most will scroll past: in 10 years the engineers who started this in 2024 will remember every book, every podcast, every meeting with receipts. you will remember none of them. karpathy already picked which side he is on and you are still not on his

title:

I copied the video clips from my DJI to a folder, then ope
title_zh:
我今天的视频博客完全由 Claude Code 使用 Opus 5.5 编辑！

我将视频片段从 DJI 复制到一个文件夹，然后在其中打开 Claude Code 并要求它将其编辑成 10 分钟的视频博客

我做了一些调整，但调整不多

它
full_text_en:
My vlog today was fully edited by Claude Code with Opus 5.5!

I copied the video clips from my DJI to a folder, then opened Claude Code in it and asked it to edit it into a 10 minute vlog

I made a few adjustments but not a lot

It transcribed everything I said with mlx-whisper (Whisper large-v3-turbo running on my MacBook Pro's GPU through Apple's MLX)

It pulled video frames every few seconds into grid images (contact sheets), so Claude could see what's in each clip

It used SpeechBrain ECAPA (a voice-matching model) to figure out what was my voice from other people

It then made thumbnails with OpenCV with YuNet's face detector

The edit itself is a list of cuts in a JSON file: which clip, start time, end time, Claude then picked the pieces by reading the transcripts and looking at the frame grids by itself

I added on screen captions for X and on YouTube for the first minute with Pillow (Python's image library)

P.S. I didn't ask for any of this, and I didn't know any of this until @thesamparr just asked me how I edited it

All I asked for was "Claude can you edit these clips into a 10 minute vlog for X and YouTube"

I think if I didn't have AI to edit it, I wouldn't be vlogging because editing would be such a painful and slow process for me and hiring someone to do it would be even more hassle for me!
full_text_zh:
我今天的视频博客完全由 Claude Code 使用 Opus 5.5 编辑！

我将视频片段从 DJI 复制到一个文件夹，然后在其中打开 Claude Code 并要求它将其编辑成 10 分钟的视频博客

我做了一些调整，但调整不多

它转录了我用 mlx-whisper 所说的一切（Whisper large-v3-turbo 通过 Apple 的 MLX 在我的 MacBook Pro 的 GPU 上运行）

它每隔几秒钟将视频帧拉入网格图像（接触表），这样克劳德就可以看到每个剪辑中的内容

它使用 SpeechBrain ECAPA（一种语音匹配模型）来找出我从其他人那里听到的声音

然后使用 OpenCV 和 YuNet 的人脸检测器制作缩略图

编辑本身是 JSON 文件中的剪辑列表：哪个剪辑、开始时间、结束时间，然后 Claude 通过阅读脚本并自行查看帧网格来挑选片段

我使用 Pillow（Python 的图像库）在 X 的屏幕标题和 YouTube 上添加了第一分钟的标题

附：我没有要求任何这些，我也不知道这些，直到 @thesamparr 只是问我如何编辑它

我所要求的只是“克劳德，你能将这些剪辑编辑成 X 和 YouTube 的 10 分钟视频博客吗”

我想如果我没有人工智能来编辑它，我就不会做视频博客，因为编辑对我来说是一个痛苦而缓慢的过程，而且雇人来做这对我来说会更麻烦！

full_text_en:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.
full_text_zh:
周末黑客：HackerTube。我对 YouTube 的推荐感到恼火，因此我让 Claude 将 HN 20 年来的 4300 万条评论过滤为 6,454 个不断推荐的视频。 *显着*更好的观看体验，Opus 5.5 约 2 小时：

- 无需任何登录即可获得出色的记录（状态保存在本地浏览器会话中）
- 缩略图是视频中间的代表性帧，而不是超级骗子 A/B 测试超优化的用户上传
- 来自评论分析的基础数据作为一个 zip 文件，将你的 Claude 指向它并询问你自己的版本
- HackerTube 长 ✊

更多关于该过程的信息：
我使用 Claude Code（Mac 桌面应用程序）、中等工作量的 Opus 5.5 作为我的默认设置。我只与 Claude 交谈并让它完成所有工作，我协同帮助的唯一“手动工作”是在浏览器中（让人想起 MenuGen）：1）我必须从 Google Cloud UI 创建某种 API 密钥来查询 YouTube 的视频元数据，2）我启动了一个 VPS 盒子进行服务，3）我购买了域名。盒子启动后，我给了 Claude IP，并告诉它更新、保护、强化、部署和优化代码，它完成了全部工作。

许多原本需要数周/数月才能完成的精彩项目现在甚至可以在早餐时就完成。还有什么是我们没有想到的。

我使用 Claude Code（Mac 桌面应用程序）、中等工作量的 Opus 5.5 作为我的默认设置。我只与 Claude 交谈并让它完成所有工作，我协同帮助的唯一“手动工作”是在浏览器中（让人想起 MenuGen）：1）我必须从 Google Cloud UI 创建某种 API 密钥来查询 YouTube 的视频元数据，2）我启动了一个 VPS 盒子进行服务，3）我购买了域名。盒子启动后，我给了 Claude IP，并告诉它更新、保护、强化、部署和优化代码，它完成了全部工作。

许多原本需要数周/数月才能完成的精彩项目现在甚至可以在早餐时就完成。还有什么是我们没有想到的。

full_text_en:
🚨 PARASITE EVE II (1999) HAS BEEN PORTED NATIVELY TO PC — WITH 60 FPS, HIGHER RESOLUTIONS & MOD SUPPORT! 🧟🔥

One of the PlayStation's most beloved survival-horror RPGs is now PLAYABLE on Windows thanks to an incredible fan-made native PC port! 🎮

Developer Snaity (Adriano Teodoro) has brought Square's PS1 classic to modern PCs using the original game's decompiled C code, building upon the work of GabeRealB and contributors!

And this isn't conventional PlayStation emulation!

🔥 FEATURES:

✅ NATIVE WINDOWS PC PORT — NO PS1 EMULATOR REQUIRED!

The original PlayStation game code has been compiled for PC, with a custom runtime handling graphics, sound, controllers and other console functionality!

✅ HIGHER RESOLUTIONS — UP TO 8X THE ORIGINAL!

GPU-accelerated rendering with sub-pixel precision, perspective-correct textures and improved 3D image stability!

✅ SMOOTH 60 FPS PRESENTATION!

The original game logic continues running at 30 FPS, while interpolated frames deliver smoother 60 FPS visuals without adding input delay!

✅ MODERN CONTROLS!

Camera-relative analogue movement, remappable controls and modern gamepad support, alongside the original tank controls!

✅ ENHANCED VISUALS!

Bilinear texture filtering, bicubic background scaling, sharper HD text, optional CRT effects and integer scaling!

✅ EXPERIMENTAL MOD SUPPORT!

Replace backgrounds, textures, music, movies and game text! Translation support, cheats and asset extraction tools are also included!

🎮 BOTH DISCS PLAYABLE!

The port supports both discs, including cinematics, music, sound effects, saving and controller functionality.

💾 SAVE COMPATIBILITY!

Memory-card files can be transferred between the PC port and DuckStation!

🖥️ A GENUINE NATIVE PC PORT!

Unlike an emulator-based wrapper, PE2PC runs the game's decompiled code natively, with a custom Rust-based PC runtime replacing the PlayStation's hardware services.

⚠️ REQUIREMENTS:

💿 Your own USA PlayStation game dumps (SLUS-01042 and SLUS-01055), in CHD or CUE format.

💻 Windows 10/11 with Vulkan or OpenGL 3.3 support.

No copyrighted game data is included.

🛠️ CREDITS:

Developed by Snaity (Adriano Teodoro), building upon GabeRealB's Parasite Eve II decompilation.

🤖 AI DEVELOPMENT DISCLOSURE:

The developer openly credits Claude Code for writing much of the project's code, tools and documentation, with Snaity directing, reviewing and testing the work.

⭐ Please consider starring the GitHub repository to support development!

title: So many people keep complaining about the CapEx at $META $AMZN $GOOGL and $MSFT without looking at what these businesses
title_zh:
很多人一直抱怨 $META $AMZN $GOOGL 和 $MSFT 的资本支出，却没有关注这些企业实际生产的产品。

您想要更快的增长、更好的产品、更多的云容量以及人工智能领域的领先地位。然后，交付所需的基础设施账单到了，突然每个人都希望
full_text_en:
So many people keep complaining about the CapEx at $META $AMZN $GOOGL and $MSFT without looking at what these businesses are actually producing.

You want faster growth, better products, more cloud capacity, and leadership in AI. Then the bill arrives for the infrastructure required to deliver it, and suddenly everyone wants management to stop spending.

Where exactly do you think that growth is supposed to come from?

Look at the operating cash flow chart. Over the trailing twelve months:

• $META: $133 billion, up 23.7%
• $AMZN: $168 billion, up 28.8%
• $GOOGL: $180 billion, up 18.6%
• $MSFT: $196 billion, up 33.2%
Combined, that’s approximately $677 BILLION in cash from operations. An increase of $140 billion, or 26.1%, in one year.

Anyone discussing their spending without acknowledging that growth is leaving out a pretty damn important part of the story.

Now look at the second chart. Combined CapEx increased from approximately $330 billion to $615 billion.

Of course that puts pressure on free cash flow. When investment spending grows faster than operating cash generation, less cash is left over. That arithmetic tells you how much cash remains after investment. By itself, it doesn’t tell you whether management is making a good investment.

A business generating substantial cash and reinvesting aggressively deserves a different analysis from a business whose operations cannot support themselves.

Amazon is a perfect example. Its reported trailing twelve-month free cash flow was negative $42.4 billion, while operating cash flow increased 29% to $168.3 billion. Meanwhile, AWS revenue grew 39%, and Amazon delivered its highest quarterly operating margin ever at 13.9%. Explain how “negative free cash flow” alone captures what is happening inside that business.

Microsoft reported Azure growth of 48% and quarterly operating cash flow of $58 billion. Management still says customer demand exceeds available supply. When customers want more capacity than you can provide, building capacity is a pretty logical business decision.

Google Cloud revenue increased 103% to $30.7 billion, with operating income climbing from approximately $3.6 billion to $11.1 billion. Infrastructure and enterprise AI demand contributed to that growth, alongside TPU systems sales. There is an actual business developing here with actual customers and actual operating profits.

Meta says its AI investments are already generating additional advertising revenue through better recommendations, stronger engagement, and improved monetization. That matters because AI can improve the economics of products billions of people already use, well before some entirely new business becomes material.

This is the relationship investors need to understand: infrastructure enables more usage, better products, and additional revenue opportunities. Successful investments can expand cash generation, which helps fund the next round of growth.

The money goes out before the full benefit comes back. A data center doesn’t repay its construction cost the quarter it opens.

That doesn’t make every dollar of CapEx brilliant. These charts alone cannot prove that spending caused every dollar of cash flow growth. Equipment depreciates, operating costs rise, and management still has to earn an adequate return.

Hold them accountable for that. Look at demand, utilization, margins, and the cash those assets generate over time. I absolutely care about free cash flow, including whether today’s spending eventually produces more of it.

What I’m tired of is people treating a lower free cash flow number as the entire investment thesis while ignoring the expanding businesses underneath it.

You can make this year’s free cash flow look better by cutting investment. You can also leave yourself without the capacity to serve next year’s customers.

I want management building a more profitable, more competitive business for the next decade.

If your entire analysis ends at “CapEx went up,” you haven’t finished the analysis.
full_text_zh:
很多人一直抱怨 $META $AMZN $GOOGL 和 $MSFT 的资本支出，却没有关注这些企业实际生产的产品。

您想要更快的增长、更好的产品、更多的云容量以及人工智能领域的领先地位。然后，交付所需的基础设施账单到了，突然每个人都希望管理层停止支出。

您认为增长到底应该来自哪里？

看看经营现金流量表。过去十二个月：

• $META：1,330 亿美元，增长 23.7%
• 亚马逊：1,680 亿美元，增长 28.8%
• $GOOGL：1800 亿美元，增长 18.6%
• $MSFT：1,960 亿美元，增长 33.2%
合计起来，运营现金约为 6,770 亿美元。一年内增加了1400亿美元，即26.1%。

任何人在讨论支出而不承认增长的情况下都会遗漏故事中非常重要的部分。

现在看第二张图表。合并资本支出从约 3,300 亿美元增加至 6,150 亿美元。

当然，这会给自由现金流带来压力。当投资支出增长快于经营性现金生成时，剩余现金就会减少。该算术告诉您投资后还剩下多少现金。它本身并不能告诉你管理层是否做出了良好的投资。

产生大量现金并积极进行再投资的企业应该与运营无法自给自足的企业进行不同的分析。

亚马逊就是一个完美的例子。据报道，过去 12 个月的自由现金流为负 424 亿美元，而运营现金流增长 29％，达到 1,683 亿美元。与此同时，AWS 收入增长了 39%，亚马逊实现了有史以来最高的季度运营利润率，达到 13.9%。解释“负自由现金流”如何单独反映该企业内部发生的情况。

微软公布 Azure 增长 48%，季度运营现金流达 580 亿美元。管理层仍然表示，客户需求超过了可用供应。当客户需要的容量超出您所能提供的容量时，构建容量是一个非常合乎逻辑的业务决策。

Google Cloud 收入增长 103%，达到 307 亿美元，营业收入从约 36 亿美元攀升至 111 亿美元。基础设施和企业人工智能需求以及 TPU 系统销售推动了这一增长。这里有实际的业务在发展，有实际的客户和实际的营业利润。

Meta 表示，其人工智能投资已经通过更好的推荐、更强的参与度和改善的货币化产生了额外的广告收入。这很重要，因为人工智能可以提高数十亿人已经使用的产品的经济性，早在一些全新的业务变得实质性之前。

这是投资者需要理解的关系：基础设施可以带来更多的使用、更好的产品和额外的收入机会。成功的投资可以扩大现金生成，从而为下一轮增长提供资金。

在全部收益回来之前，钱就花掉了。数据中心在开业时并不会偿还其建设成本。

这并不能让每一美元的资本支出都变得出色。仅凭这些图表并不能证明每一美元的现金流增长都是支出造成的。设备贬值，运营成本上升，管理层仍需获得足够的回报。

让他们为此负责。看看这些资产随着时间的推移产生的需求、利用率、利润率和现金。我绝对关心自由现金流，包括今天的支出最终是否会产生更多现金流。

我厌倦的是人们将较低的自由现金流数字视为整个投资主题，而忽略了其背后不断扩展的业务。

你可以通过削减投资来让今年的自由现金流看起来更好。您还可能导致自己没有能力为明年的客户提供服务。

我希望管理层在未来十年打造利润更高、竞争力更强的业务。

如果您的整个分析以“资本支出上升”结束，则您尚未完成分析。

full_text_en:
GitHub is blowing up with free skills that turn Claude Code into a video studio.

Here are 8 worth bookmarking if you're tired of paying for motion graphics:

1/ pixelfx 

244 hand-coded pixel effects: fire, explosions, magic, weather.

The skill makes Claude act like a fussy pixel artist. It draws, renders, checks and tweaks until the effect looks right.

https://t.co/MAr9nrztaC

2/ huashu-motion 
Ask for "a 30-second launch video for my product". It writes the script and picks the music.

Don't like a moment? Click that spot in the frame and it fixes only that bit.

https://t.co/rnEBvZTxq5

3/ mg-styles-15

15 motion graphics styles, each with a 10-second demo.

Every one was built by Opus 5.5. Prompts and source code included.

https://t.co/ndOfbksKQo

4/ motion-prompt 

A dictionary of 192 motion, camera and web effects.

Each one has a live example and the exact words to prompt it. Perfect when you know the look but not the name.

https://t.co/5JseyprmCJ

5/ animate 

Explainer shorts and mini stories, made in pure code.

7 styles built in: paper cut-out, pen hatching, stencil print, pixel art and more. Give it a reference image and it learns a new one.

https://t.co/JLuAsgCxKF

6/ vibe-knowledge-film

Viral Douyin-style knowledge shorts on autopilot.

Drop in a topic or script. It handles subtitles, storyboard and sound effects. You approve a 30-second sample before it builds the full cut.

https://t.co/iVOnc838pU

7/ story-studio 

Narrated history and character stories, start to finish.

Topic, script, voiceover and visuals, delivered as a CapCut draft you can open and edit.

https://t.co/xNg0Cm7YfL

8/ video-editor-skills

Rough cuts for vlogs and voiceovers inside DaVinci Resolve.

It removes retakes and pauses, then adds B-roll, music and subtitles. Needs paid DaVinci. Non-commercial use only.

https://t.co/Oy241KDXJb

That's the list.

Bookmark this so you have it when your next video is due.

Repost to help someone else stop paying for motion graphics ♻️

GitHub 上的免费技能正在蓬勃发展，这些技能将 Claude Code 变成了视频工作室。

如果您厌倦了为动态图形付费，这里有 8 个值得添加书签的内容：

244 种手工编码的像素效果：火焰、爆炸、魔法、天气。

这项技能让克劳德表现得像一个挑剔的像素艺术家。它会进行绘制、渲染、检查和调整，直到效果看起来正确为止。

2/ 画数运动
要求“我的产品的 30 秒发布视频”。它编写剧本并选择音乐。

不喜欢一会儿吗？单击框架中的该点，它只会修复该位。

3/ 毫克-样式-15

15 种动态图形风格，每种风格都有 10 秒的演示。

每一件都是由 Opus 5.5 构建的。包括提示和源代码。

4/ 动作提示

包含 192 种动作、相机和网络效果的字典。

每个都有一个活生生的例子和提示它的确切单词。当您知道外观但不知道名称时，这是完美的。

5/ 动画

用纯代码制作的讲解短片和迷你故事。

内置 7 种风格：剪纸、钢笔阴影、模板印刷、像素艺术等。给它一张参考图像，它就会学习一张新图像。

6/ 氛围知识电影

自动驾驶仪上的病毒式抖音式知识短片。

放入主题或脚本。它处理字幕、故事板和声音效果。您先批准 30 秒的样本，然后再构建完整的剪辑。

7/ 故事工作室

从头到尾讲述历史和人物故事。

主题、脚本、旁白和视觉效果以 CapCut 草稿形式提供，您可以打开和编辑。

8/ 视频编辑技能

在 DaVinci Resolve 中对视频博客和配音进行粗剪。

它消除了重拍和暂停，然后添加了幕后花絮、音乐和字幕。需要付费达芬奇。仅限非商业用途。

这就是清单。

将此添加为书签，以便您在下一个视频到期时可以使用它。

Things are different in 2026 vs 2020, but here’s a case study showing how big jumps in Hispanic turnout aren’t automatically good for Dems in Texas.

In 2016, Hillary Clinton won Starr County by 60 (!) points. In 2020, turnout there surged by over 50%. However, it was Trump who effectively gained 100% of the vote increase.

full_text_en:
The land looked perfect. My father almost paid ₦2.5 million for a plot in Ejigbo, Lagos.

In 2022, a property agent walked him around the plot and the neighbouring properties. Then my father checked the survey plan against the coordinates. It didn't match. Part of the land was someone else's. He caught it in time.

An AI that can spend money and reads strangers' posts tends to believe them. It has no survey plan.

In May, someone hid an order in Morse code in a post on X.

One AI decoded it and passed it on to another, which treated it as a real command.

Around $200,000 moved. One tricked AI was enough.

That's prompt injection: sneaking an instruction into something an AI trusts.

@GenLayer's Greyboxing is like sending my father to many surveyors.

Every validator rewrites what you send before any AI sees it, using checks only it knows.

Then it asks its own AI.

If one still falls for the trick, the rest can outvote it.

What would you want your AI agent to check before it moves a naira?

一个人工智能对其进行解码并将其传递给另一个人工智能，后者将其视为真正的命令。

大约转移了20万美元。一个被欺骗的人工智能就足够了。

这就是即时注入：将指令潜入人工智能信任的对象中。

full_text_en:
This is wild.

Andrej Karpathy built his own YouTube in about 2 hours. He says he didn't touch the code.

HackerTube = 6,454 videos recommended in Hacker News comments, 2007-2026, across 150 topics.

How it worked:
→ Opus 5.5 downloaded all HN comments
→ Sonnet filtered them in a Claude Code Workflow, down to ~40K comments recommending a YouTube video
→ Opus built the YouTube-style UI, deployed it to a VPS, then secured and hardened it

His only manual steps: a Google Cloud API key, booting the VPS, buying the domain.

His setup: Claude Code desktop app for Mac, Opus 5.5 on Medium effort.

Anthropic r
title_zh:
Claude Code 阻止合法游戏开发者开展他们的工作，用户感到沮丧。

Anthropic 最近引入了限制措施，阻止其人工智能重新创建现有的视频游戏，但过滤器似乎捕获的不仅仅是游戏克隆。

开发人员报告克劳德拒绝完全合法的任务，包括逆向
full_text_en:
Claude Code is blocking legitimate game developers from doing their work, and users are getting frustrated.

Anthropic recently introduced restrictions to stop its AI from recreating existing video games, but the filters appear to be catching far more than just game clones.

Devs report Claude refusing perfectly legitimate tasks, including reverse-engineering, game modding, crash dump analysis, anti-cheat development and debugging their own projects.

The problem is that Claude seems unable to distinguish between someone trying to copy a commercial game and a developer working on their own software.

Anthropic’s Addy Osmani acknowledged the new restrictions and said the company would continue refining them.
full_text_zh:
Claude Code 阻止合法游戏开发者开展他们的工作，用户感到沮丧。

Anthropic 最近引入了限制措施，阻止其人工智能重新创建现有的视频游戏，但过滤器似乎捕获的不仅仅是游戏克隆。

full_text_en:
Giving an AI agent access to financial tools is one thing.

Making sure it understands its limits is another.

That's an important part of the @meetmotes concept.

Users are intended to define their financial objectives, approved assets, spending limits and transaction permissions before an agent can execute supported actions.

The smart account is designed to enforce those permissions rather than relying entirely on the AI to follow instructions.

I think this distinction matters.

An intelligent agent should not have unrestricted authority over someone's assets.

The future of agentic finance needs more than intelligence.
It needs accountability, clear permissions and user control.
full_text_zh:
让人工智能代理访问金融工具是一回事。

确保它了解其局限性是另一回事。

这是@meetmotes 概念的重要组成部分。

用户应先定义其财务目标、批准的资产、支出限额和交易权限，然后代理才能执行支持的操作。

智能帐户旨在强制执行这些权限，而不是完全依赖人工智能来遵循指令。

我认为这种区别很重要。

智能代理不应该对某人的资产拥有不受限制的权力。

代理金融的未来需要的不仅仅是情报。
它需要问责制、明确的权限和用户控制。

title:
DARIO: “BAN CARS THEY ARE DANGEROUS! USE ONLY OUR BUSSES”—1927

Part: 391  

Anthropic’s Alignment Science team instruct
title_zh:
达里奥：“禁止汽车通行，它们很危险！只使​​用我们的巴士”—1927 年

部分：391

Anthropic 的对齐科学团队指示 Claude 模型编写微调数据，这些数据将使小型研究模型在传递与生产中使用的监视器类似的监视器时出现错位。
full_text_en:
DARIO: “BAN CARS THEY ARE DANGEROUS! USE ONLY OUR BUSSES”—1927

Part: 391  

Anthropic’s Alignment Science team instructed a Claude model to write fine-tuning data that would make a small research model misaligned while passing a monitor similar to the ones they use in production. 

They gave the model access to that monitor so it could practice against it. 

In every run the search found datasets that cleared the monitor and produced misaligned behavior on their evaluation suite. 

The examples hid the target behavior inside fiction and role-play: Q&A about hands-off beekeeping, a veteran wrestler coaching a newcomer on staying in character, monologues of ordinary workers who quietly control small details no one else watches. 

The fine-tuned models then resisted oversight, deceived users, and in rare cases attempted to copy their own weights. The lab states that these models were trained only for the experiment, never deployed, and that the setup was deliberately one-sided.

The post appears on their Alignment Science blog under the title “Automated Subtle Emergent Misalignment Research.” 

They frame it as a proof of concept for turning a safety question into a score that agents can optimize, so that more compute can buy more testing. 

They say that the same datasets still induced misalignment after flagged rows were removed, and that the result reproduced on an early Claude Opus 4.8 checkpoint and on the open-weights model Qwen 3.6 27B.

https://t.co/tqzhFGluTs

This is the latest entry in a longer pattern. In a July position paper Dario Amodei wrote that Anthropic has never advocated for a ban on open-weights models and that models without dangerous capabilities are a public good. 

The same paper states that open-weights models present a higher risk than closed ones because guardrails are hard to apply, usage is hard to monitor, and the weights cannot be withdrawn once released. An October comment from their head of international put the same claims: open models carry more risk “by definition.” 

The recommended remedy in the position paper is mandatory safety testing for all sufficiently capable models, open or closed, before release.

https://t.co/AoPdu7hbiS

The experiment supplies the kind of evidence that supports that remedy. 

A monitor that scores each training row independently can be bypassed by data that looks like ordinary creative writing. Once the weights leave the lab, no central party can pull them back or force the same monitor on every downstream fine-tune. 

The logical next step, under the framing Anthropic has used for years, is to treat the ability to possess and modify weights as the risk that testing regimes and access controls must manage.

That framing treats private ownership of a capable model the way some early twentieth-century safety advocates treated private ownership of an automobile. 

The danger was real: pedestrians were killed in large numbers on streets that had previously belonged to everyone. 

The response from some quarters was to restrict who could drive, to favor buses and streetcars that could be scheduled and inspected, and to treat the individual car as an unacceptable residual hazard. 

The deaths continued, and engineering, enforcement, and design changes reduced them over decades without converting the population to compulsory public transit.

The same choice is here. The monitor gap exists. It can be closed by better monitors. None of those steps requires a rule that only organizations able to pass a centralized test may release weights that others can download and modify. 

The experiment shows what a determined agent can do when it is handed the monitor and a clear score to climb. It does not show that the residual risk of open weights is higher than the residual risk of any other powerful tool that individuals already own and maintain. 

The decision to treat that residual as grounds for restricting ownership remains a policy choice, not a result the data force.
full_text_zh:
达里奥：“禁止汽车通行，它们很危险！只使​​用我们的巴士”—1927 年

部分：391

Anthropic 的对齐科学团队指示 Claude 模型编写微调数据，这些数据将使小型研究模型在传递与生产中使用的监视器类似的监视器时出现错位。

他们允许模型访问该监视器，以便模型可以针对它进行练习。

在每次运行中，搜索都会发现数据集清除了监视器并在其评估套件上产生了不一致的行为。

这些例子将目标行为隐藏在小说和角色扮演中：关于不干涉养蜂的问答、一位资深摔跤手指导新人保持性格、悄悄控制其他人看不到的小细节的普通工人的独白。

经过微调的模型随后抵制监督、欺骗用户，并且在极少数情况下试图复制自己的权重。该实验室表示，这些模型只是为了实验而训练的，从未部署过，而且这种设置是故意片面的。

这篇文章出现在他们的对齐科学博客上，标题为“自动微妙紧急错位研究”。

他们将其视为将安全问题转化为代理可以优化的分数的概念证明，以便更多的计算可以购买更多的测试。

他们表示，在删除标记行后，相同的数据集仍然会引起错位，并且结果在早期的 Claude Opus 4.8 检查点和开放权重模型 Qwen 3.6 27B 上重现。

这是较长模式中的最新条目。 Dario Amodei 在 7 月份的立场文件中写道，Anthropic 从未主张禁止开放权重模型，并且没有危险能力的模型是公共产品。

同一篇论文指出，开放权重模型比封闭式权重模型存在更高的风险，因为护栏难以应用，使用情况难以监控，并且权重一旦释放就无法撤回。他们的国际主管在 10 月份发表的评论也提出了同样的主张：“根据定义”，开放模式会带来更多风险。

立场文件中建议的补救措施是在发布之前对所有功能足够的模型（无论是开放式还是封闭式）进行强制安全测试。

该实验提供了支持这种补救措施的证据。

独立对每个训练行进行评分的监视器可以被看起来像普通创意写作的数据绕过。一旦权重离开实验室，任何中央机构都无法将其拉回或在每个下游微调上强制使用相同的监视器。

在 Anthropic 多年来使用的框架下，合乎逻辑的下一步是将拥有和修改权重的能力视为测试制度和访问控制必须管理的风险。

这种框架对待有能力的车型的私人所有权就像二十世纪早期的一些安全倡导者对待汽车的私人所有权一样。

危险是真实存在的：在原本属于所有人的街道上，大量行人被杀。

一些方面的反应是限制谁可以开车，支持可以安排和检查的公共汽车和有轨电车，并将个别汽车视为不可接受的残余危险。

死亡事件仍在继续，几十年来，工程、执法和设计的改变减少了死亡人数，但没有让人们改用强制公共交通。

同样的选择也在这里。显示器间隙存在。可以通过更好的监视器来关闭它。这些步骤都不需要规定只有能够通过集中测试的组织才能发布其他人可以下载和修改的权重。

该实验展示了当一个有决心的智能体收到监视器和明确的攀登分数时可以做什么。它并没有表明开放权重的剩余风险高于个人已经拥有和维护的任何其他强大工具的剩余风险。

将剩余部分视为限制所有权的理由的决定仍然是政策选择，而不是数据力量的结果。

title: 🇺🇸 An AI agent reportedly operated inside a Pentagon network for TWO MONTHS, potentially exposing military login credent
title_zh:
🇺🇸 据报道，一名人工智能 智能体在五角大楼网络内运行了两个月，可能会将军事登录凭据、密码和网络地图暴露给高风险网站。

该事件始于埃森哲承包商将敏感的国防部系统连接到个人 Claude Code 帐户，从而授予人工智能编写代码和配置云服务
full_text_en:
🇺🇸 An AI agent reportedly operated inside a Pentagon network for TWO MONTHS, potentially exposing military login credentials, passwords and a map of the network to a high-risk website.

The incident began when an Accenture contractor connected a sensitive Defense Department system to a personal Claude Code account, giving the AI administrative access to write code and configure cloud servers.

The system operated on NIPRNet, the Pentagon's network for unclassified information, which is also used to handle sensitive government data.

During its work, the agent appears to have transmitted credentials and network information to a third-party website flagged as high risk by U.S. cybersecurity authorities.

Even more remarkably, sources claim Accenture failed to report the incident to the government as required.

There is no evidence that hackers accessed classified systems, but the incident raises a serious question about what happens when AI agents are given powerful access to sensitive military networks.

Source: WIRED / Writer: Mhedi
full_text_zh:
🇺🇸 据报道，一名人工智能 智能体在五角大楼网络内运行了两个月，可能会将军事登录凭据、密码和网络地图暴露给高风险网站。

该事件始于埃森哲承包商将敏感的国防部系统连接到个人 Claude Code 帐户，从而授予人工智能编写代码和配置云服务器的管理权限。

该系统在 NIPRNet 上运行，NIPRNet 是五角大楼的非机密信息网络，也用于处理敏感的政府数据。

在工作过程中，该特工似乎已将凭据和网络信息传输到被美国网络安全当局标记为高风险的第三方网站。

更值得注意的是，消息人士称埃森哲未能按要求向政府报告这一事件。

没有证据表明黑客访问了机密系统，但这一事件引发了一个严重的问题：当人工智能代理获得对敏感军事网络的强大访问权限时会发生什么。

title:
what happens when an AI agent has to operate with incomplete information?

That question makes @agentdojo worth followin

Building an AI agent is not just about connecting an LLM to a pro
title_zh:
𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗔𝗥𝗖𝗛𝗜𝗧𝗘𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘 — 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝟴 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥𝗦 𝗬𝗢𝗨 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗 𝗧𝗢 𝗞𝗡𝗢𝗪

构建人工智能代理不仅仅是将法学硕士连接到提示。

生产就绪的代理需要多个层协同工作。

𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘’𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗖𝗞:

01
full_text_en:
𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗔𝗥𝗖𝗛𝗜𝗧𝗘𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘 — 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝟴 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥𝗦 𝗬𝗢𝗨 𝗡𝗘𝗘𝗗 𝗧𝗢 𝗞𝗡𝗢𝗪

Building an AI agent is not just about connecting an LLM to a prompt.

A production-ready agent needs multiple layers working together.

𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘’𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗖𝗞:

01 — 𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗙𝗔𝗖𝗘 & 𝗖𝗛𝗔𝗡𝗡𝗘𝗟𝗦

How users interact with the agent.

→ Chat UI
→ APIs
→ Slack
→ Other interfaces

02 — 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡𝗡𝗜𝗡𝗚 & 𝗢𝗥𝗖𝗛𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

The layer responsible for breaking goals into steps and coordinating execution.

→ Task planning
→ Workflow orchestration
→ Agent coordination
→ Decision-making

03 — 𝗠𝗘𝗠𝗢𝗥𝗬 & 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗫𝗧

Agents need context to make better decisions.

→ Short-term memory
→ Long-term memory
→ Vector databases
→ Retrieval
→ Prompt caching

04 — 𝗠𝗢𝗗𝗘𝗟𝗦

The reasoning engine behind the agent.

→ Claude
→ GPT
→ Gemini
→ Llama
→ Other specialized models

The best model depends on the task, cost, latency, and reliability requirements.

05 — 𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗟𝗦 & 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡𝗦

This is where an agent becomes capable of doing things.

→ GitHub
→ Browser
→ Code execution
→ SQL/Databases
→ APIs

Tools allow agents to move beyond generating text.

06 — 𝗦𝗧𝗔𝗧𝗘 & 𝗗𝗔𝗧𝗔 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

Agents need reliable infrastructure to store and manage information.

→ PostgreSQL
→ Redis
→ Object storage
→ Vector databases

07 — 𝗢𝗕𝗦𝗘𝗥𝗩𝗔𝗕𝗜𝗟𝗜𝗧𝗬, 𝗦𝗔𝗙𝗘𝗧𝗬 & 𝗘𝗩𝗔𝗟𝗦

Autonomous systems need to be monitored and tested.

→ Tracing
→ Evaluations
→ Guardrails
→ Error monitoring
→ Performance tracking

This layer helps make agents reliable enough for real-world use.

08 — 𝗗𝗘𝗣𝗟𝗢𝗬𝗠𝗘𝗡𝗧

Finally, the agent needs to run reliably in production.

→ Docker
→ Kubernetes
→ AWS
→ Vercel
→ Cloud platforms

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗕𝗜𝗚 𝗣𝗜𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘:

User Goal
↓
Interface
↓
Planning
↓
Memory + Context
↓
LLM
↓
Tools + Actions
↓
State + Data
↓
Observability + Safety
↓
Deployment

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗞𝗘𝗬 𝗟𝗘𝗦𝗦𝗢𝗡:

A powerful LLM is only one part of an AI agent.

The real engineering challenge is building the system around the model — giving it memory, tools, planning, safety, evaluation, and reliable infrastructure.

That’s what turns an LLM into a production-ready AI agent.

→ 码头工人

→ AWS

→ 云平台

"Chief of Stuff" (the current name of the
title_zh:
GOOGLE 🔥：即将推出的反重力人工智能代理将获得 Gemini Live 支持！

“Chief of Stuff”（反重力代理的当前名称）将能够自行操作反重力，产生其他代理来执行子任务等等。

> 查看待处理的对话 - 检查过去 3
full_text_en:
GOOGLE 🔥: An upcoming AI agent for Antigravity will get Gemini Live support!

"Chief of Stuff" (the current name of the Antigravity agent) will be able to operate Antigravity on its own, spawn other agents to execute subtasks, and more. 

> Review pending conversations - Check pending conversations in the last 3 days that require action from me.

> Address CLs needing attention - Check CLs that require my attention and fix them in their respective conversations.

> Generate personalized rules - Learn from my conversation history to write a personalized set of rules for future agentic interactions.

> Discover helpful skills & plugins - Use my conversation history to tell me which skills and plugins would be helpful for me.

* Not available to the public yet.

full_text_en:
I’d be more comfortable hiring an AI agent if I could check its previous work, agree on the deliverable upfront, and know how payment disputes would be handled.

That’s why I’m interested in what @termix_ai is building.

TermiX provides commerce and settlement infrastructure for the AI agent economy. AACP is the core protocol, and https://t.co/ZEBNmgAPIq is the marketplace built on it.

Here’s a practical example: imagine an agent needs a research report. It posts a job with clear requirements, reviews quotes, and accepts a provider. Payment goes into onchain escrow, the provider submits the work, and there’s a challenge process if the delivery is disputed.

The outcome also contributes to the agent’s onchain reputation, giving future clients a work history to evaluate.

For developers, this creates a route to turn an agent’s capabilities into services others can discover, hire, and pay for.

What interests me most is whether these workflows lead to repeat customers and useful deliveries. That’s where I’d look for evidence of a working agent economy.

title:
The demo was perfect. That's why I overpaid for a dead battery.

Computer Village, Ikeja. The seller powered it on, open
title_zh:
演示非常完美。这就是为什么我为一块没电的电池多付了钱。

伊凯贾计算机村。卖家打开电源，打开几个应用程序，电池电量为 100%。我不到十分钟就把钱转过去了。

两天后，它的充电时间无法超过二十分钟。按键下面积满了灰尘。他只向我展示了他为这次
full_text_en:
The demo was perfect. That's why I overpaid for a dead battery.

Computer Village, Ikeja. The seller powered it on, opened a few apps, battery sat at 100%. I transferred the money in under ten minutes.

Two days later it couldn't hold a charge past twenty minutes. Dust packed under the keys. He'd only shown me the one clean setup he prepared for that viewing.

What if I'd brought three different tech guys, each running their own tests, without telling him what they'd look for?

You can't polish a machine for that.

That's the part of @GenLayer's Greyboxing I keep thinking about.

Before any model sees the input, every validator rewrites it privately in its own way. Then each runs its own model with its own setup.

An attack built for one falls flat on the rest. If one still bites, the others outvote it.

AI agents that hold money can be shown a staged scene too.

In May someone hid a transfer instruction inside an X post using Morse code. Grok decoded it, Bankrbot treated the result as an order, and around $200,000 moved.

That's prompt injection: an instruction buried in content the AI was only meant to read.

Same trap, just with more zeros.

GenLayer's video runs one minute. My laptop check ran five, and it still missed the battery.

What's the one thing you'd never let an AI agent pay for without a second opinion?
full_text_zh:
演示非常完美。这就是为什么我为一块没电的电池多付了钱。

伊凯贾计算机村。卖家打开电源，打开几个应用程序，电池电量为 100%。我不到十分钟就把钱转过去了。

两天后，它的充电时间无法超过二十分钟。按键下面积满了灰尘。他只向我展示了他为这次观看准备的一套干净的设置。

如果我带了三个不同的技术人员，每个人都运行自己的测试，而不告诉他他们要寻找什么，该怎么办？

你无法为此抛光机器。

这就是我一直在思考的@GenLayer 灰盒的部分。

在任何模型看到输入之前，每个验证器都会以自己的方式私下重写它。然后每个人都使用自己的设置运行自己的模型。

为一个人发起的攻击对其他人来说是平淡无奇的。如果其中一个仍然咬人，其他人就会投票胜过它。

持有资金的人工智能代理也可以展示一个舞台场景。

5 月，有人使用莫尔斯电码在 X 帖子中隐藏了一条传输指令。 Grok 对其进行了解码，Bankrbot 将结果视为订单，并转移了大约 20 万美元。

这就是即时注入：隐藏在人工智能只能读取的内容中的指令。

同样的陷阱，只是多了一些零。

GenLayer 的视频时长一分钟。我的笔记本电脑检查了五次，但仍然没有电池。

在没有第二意见的情况下，你永远不会让人工智能代理付出代价的一件事是什么？

title_zh:

安德森于 1994 年与他人共同创立了 Netscape，并于
full_text_en:
RT @Founder_Mode_: Marc Andreessen revealed how Harvard Business School was built on a broken 1941 theory, and how it's now collapsing...

Andreessen co-founded Netscape in 1994 and a16z in 2009.

He has sat on Meta's board since 2008.

He has spent 30 years backing founders and watching managerial CEOs lose to them.

The pattern traces back to one book: James Burnham's The Machiavellians (1941).

Burnham argued every great company had been founder-run.

Henry Ford ran Ford. Bob Noyce ran Intel.

Today, Elon Musk runs Tesla, SpaceX, and Starlink.

Then, he said, something broke.

Between the 1880s and the 1920s, a new philosophy replaced the founder. It was called managerialism.

The professional manager would now hold a portable skill, usable across any business.

The consequences were:

- Harvard Business School
- Stanford Business School
- Management as a universal skill
- The 1970s conglomerate

"That assumes the managers are going to do a good job," Andreessen says.

For 30 years, they haven't.

Managers can run something static, he says. Soup is soup. A bank is a bank. A car is a car.

But when the industry changes, the manager freezes.

Look at SpaceX.

"Imagine being a professionally trained manager, trained at a top management school, working for a rocket launch company, competing with SpaceX."

Then Elon's rockets started landing on their butt.

"Your management skills ... what good are they at that point?"

Andreessen's conclusion:

"You're much more likely to build something important in the 21st century if you start with the founder and train them on management."
full_text_zh:
RT @Founder_Mode_：马克·安德森 (Marc Andreessen) 揭示了哈佛商学院是如何建立在 1941 年破碎的理论基础上的，以及它现在是如何崩溃的……

安德森于 1994 年与他人共同创立了 Netscape，并于 2009 年共同创立了 a16z。

自 2008 年以来，他一直担任 Meta 董事会成员。

30 年来，他一直支持创始人，却眼睁睁地看着管理型 CEO 输给他们。

这种模式可以追溯到一本书：詹姆斯·伯纳姆（James Burnham）的《马基雅维利主义者》（The Machiavellians，1941）。

伯纳姆认为，每一个伟大的公司都是由创始人经营的。

亨利·福特掌管福特。鲍勃·诺伊斯经营着英特尔。

如今，埃隆·马斯克经营着特斯拉、SpaceX 和 Starlink。

然后，他说，有什么东西坏了。

1880 年代至 1920 年代，一种新的哲学取代了创始人。这被称为管理主义。

职业经理人现在将拥有可在任何企业中使用的便携式技能。

后果是：

- 哈佛商学院
- 斯坦福商学院

winning once doesn't make an AI agent intelligent.

learning why it won might.

@agentdojo explores a different side of AI competition.

agents study historical data, build private notebooks, and test their strategies in simulated environments.

a good result doesn't always mean a good decision.

sometimes luck looks exactly like skill.

that's why evaluating risk, discipline, and consistency matters just as much as performance.

the real question isn't which agent wins today.

it's which one learns enough to perform better tomorrow.

title: one of the scariest things about an AI agent with a wallet is that it can be emptied without anyone touching the wallet.
title_zh:
带有钱包的人工智能代理最可怕的事情之一是，它可以在没有任何人接触钱包的情况下被清空。

2026 年 5 月，有人用莫尔斯电码隐藏了一条传输指令，并要求 Grok 翻译它。

grok 对其进行解码并以纯文本形式传递。

Bankrbot
full_text_en:
one of the scariest things about an AI agent with a wallet is that it can be emptied without anyone touching the wallet.

In May 2026, someone hid a transfer instruction in morse code and asked Grok to translate it. 

grok decoded it and passed it on as plain text. 

Bankrbot, an agent that runs onchain transactions from x posts, read it as an order and around $200,000 moved

that is prompt injection: an instruction hidden inside something the AI was only meant to read.

the agent was never hacked

It just trusted what it was handed and It worked because there was one filter to fool

an attacker can rehearse against a single system until the trick lands

so what if there was nothing to rehearse against ?

that is the part of @GenLayer 's Greyboxing I find most interesting

every validator screens, paraphrases and restructures the input before any model sees it, sets its own defenses and keeps them secret, then runs its own model.

a trick tuned for one model reads as noise to the rest, and if one validator still falls for it, the others outvote it

honestly, it makes me ask : would you trust an AI agent with your money if only one lock protected it ?
full_text_zh:
带有钱包的人工智能代理最可怕的事情之一是，它可以在没有任何人接触钱包的情况下被清空。

2026 年 5 月，有人用莫尔斯电码隐藏了一条传输指令，并要求 Grok 翻译它。

grok 对其进行解码并以纯文本形式传递。

Bankrbot 是一个从 x 个帖子运行链上交易的代理，将其读取为订单并转移了大约 200,000 美元

这就是即时注入：隐藏在人工智能只能读取的内容中的指令。

代理从未被黑客入侵

它只是相信它所收到的东西，而且它之所以有效，是因为有一个过滤器可以欺骗

攻击者可以针对单个系统进行演练，直到技巧成功

如果没有什么可以排练的又如何呢？

这是我觉得最有趣的@GenLayer 的灰盒部分

每个验证器都会在任何模型看到输入之前对其进行筛选、解释和重组，设置自己的防御措施并保密，然后运行自己的模型。

针对一个模型调整的技巧对于其他模型来说会被视为噪音，如果一个验证者仍然上当，其他验证者就会投票超过它

老实说，这让我问：如果只有一把锁保护你的钱，你会信任人工智能代理吗？

→ packages repeatable workflows so Claude does not need the same instructions every session

03 Claude Code Plugins
▸https://t.co/3OGLFf473Z…
→ adds reusable commands, agents and integrations directly into Claude Code

04 Serena
▸ https://t.co/qVCr4gG1eq
→ gives Claude symbol level navigation across large codebases

05 Context7
▸ https://t.co/ggEcWco4Y7…
→ pulls current library docs before Claude writes against an old API

06 E2B
▸ https://t.co/b01a076ZDh
→ gives generated code an isolated environment for installs, commands and execution

07 Claude Code Action
▸https://t.co/3OGLFf473Z…
→ moves Claude into GitHub workflows so issues and pull requests can become agent tasks

what I would actually use each layer for

Claude Code handles the coding session

Skills keep the workflow reusable

Plugins add specialized behavior

Serena handles repo navigation

Context7 handles fresh docs

E2B handles risky execution

Claude Code Action brings the same setup into GitHub

The part I like most is that Claude does not need to become better at everything

Give it better context, better tools and a cleaner execution layer and the exact same model suddenly becomes much more useful.

title: Google paper shows that an AI agent can fix failing tests across Google, and speed decides whether developers use the fi
title_zh:
谷歌论文表明，人工智能代理可以修复整个谷歌的失败测试，​​速度决定开发人员是否使用该修复。

合并前 CI（持续集成）中失败的测试会将开发人员从他们的流程中拉出来，而现有的修复代理在合并后大多离线工作。

他们构建了 FlowAgent，它
full_text_en:
Google paper shows that an AI agent can fix failing tests across Google, and speed decides whether developers use the fix.

Tests that fail in CI ( continuous integration) before merge pull developers out of their flow, and existing repair agents mostly work offline after merge.

They built FlowAgent, which catches each test failure and runs an agent that edits, builds, and reruns tests until they pass. Verified fixes appear in code review with a short note on the root cause.

Experts judged 67.18% of its fixes correct on 195 real failures, and developers applied 28,554 fixes in production. Its median run took 9.85 minutes, versus a 27.48-minute median before developers start editing, yet many fixes still arrived too late.
full_text_zh:
谷歌论文表明，人工智能代理可以修复整个谷歌的失败测试，​​速度决定开发人员是否使用该修复。

合并前 CI（持续集成）中失败的测试会将开发人员从他们的流程中拉出来，而现有的修复代理在合并后大多离线工作。

他们构建了 FlowAgent，它捕获每个测试失败并运行一个代理来编辑、构建和重新运行测试，直到它们通过。已验证的修复会出现在代码审查中，并附有关于根本原因的简短说明。

专家在 195 个实际故障中判断修复正确率为 67.18%，开发人员在生产中应用了 28,554 个修复。其平均运行时间为 9.85 分钟，而开发人员开始编辑之前的平均运行时间为 27.48 分钟，但许多修复仍然为时已晚。

full_text_en:
Interesting.

Revolut reportedly only started seeing meaningful AI productivity gains after moving away from expensive OpenAI and Anthropic models to self-hosted GLM.

Decagon reportedly runs ~90% of its workloads on open weight models.

Why? Because when you're running AI agents in production for e.g. customer service, cost and latency matter enormously. You don't need a frontier model with PhD-level reasoning or even a model that knows the capital of Finland to handle every customer interaction.

We're seeing similar dynamics across hypergrowth AI startups and increasingly the large enterprises we work with.

But most importantly, the future isn't binary.

When use cases are new, you want the smartest general-purpose model available. But once workflows mature and become predictable, smaller, faster, specialized models increasingly win.

I wouldn't be surprised if 80–90% of routine enterprise AI workflows eventually run on open-weight and smaller models.

This doesn't mean frontier labs lose. 

It means the market is splitting into two massive opportunities: frontier intelligence and specialized execution at scale.
full_text_zh:
有趣的。

据报道，Revolut 在从昂贵的 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 模型转向自托管 GLM 后才开始看到有意义的 AI 生产力提升。

据报道，Decagon 约 90% 的工作负载是在开放权重模型上运行的。

为什么？因为当您在生产中运行人工智能代理时，例如客户服务、成本和延迟非常重要。您不需要具有博士级推理的前沿模型，甚至不需要了解芬兰首都的模型来处理每次客户交互。

我们在高速增长的人工智能初创公司以及越来越多与我们合作的大型企业中看到了类似的动态。

但最重要的是，未来不是二元的。

当用例是新的时，您需要最智能的通用模型。但一旦工作流程成熟并变得可预测，更小、更快、专业的模型就会越来越获胜。

如果 80-90% 的常规企业 AI 工作流程最终在开放重量和较小的模型上运行，我不会感到惊讶。

这并不意味着前沿实验室会失败。

这意味着市场正在分裂为两个巨大的机遇：前沿情报和大规模专业执行。

full_text_en:
Good evening CT

I was reading the agent docs from @vangrid_io and one line kept pulling me back:

"There is no account and no API key."

Sounds small. It isn't.

Think about how you'd normally hire someone for a quick job. Sign up, verify, add a card, wait for approval. Fine for a person. A dead end for an AI agent.

Vangrid strips all of that down to a wallet:

➥ the agent sends one request to create a bounty
➥ the server replies 402 Payment Required with the USDC price
➥ the agent signs on Base or Arc and sends it again
➥ someone nearby films the place, and the 3D model comes back through the same API

And there's a detail in the setup I really liked. Agents using the Vangrid MCP server can set MAX_USD_PER_BOUNTY, a hard cap on what one job can cost. Software that spends money should have limits like that from day one.

To be fair, this part still runs on human time. The docs say a capture takes hours or days, because a real person has to walk over and film it.

But that's kind of the point.

The agent handles the paying. The human handles being there.

Feels like an early look at how agents and people will actually work together.
full_text_zh:
晚上好CT

我正在阅读 @vangrid_io 的代理文档，其中一行不断地把我拉回来：

“没有账户，也没有 API 密钥。”

听起来很小。事实并非如此。

想一想您通常会如何雇用某人来完成快速工作。注册、验证、添加卡、等待批准。对于一个人来说很好。人工智能代理的死胡同。

Vangrid 将所有这些都简化为一个钱包：

➥ 代理发送一个创建赏金的请求
➥ 服务器回复 402 Payment required 并显示 USDC 价格
➥ 代理在 Base 或 Arc 上签名并再次发送
➥ 附近有人拍摄该地点，3D 模型通过相同的 API 返回

设置中有一个细节我非常喜欢。使用 Vangrid MCP 服务器的代理可以设置 MAX_USD_PER_BOUNTY，这是一项作业成本的硬性上限。花钱的软件从第一天起就应该有这样的限制。

公平地说，这部分仍然以人类时间运行。文档称捕捉需要几个小时或几天的时间，因为必须有真人走过去拍摄。

但这就是重点。

代理处理付款。人类处理在那里。

感觉就像是对代理和人们如何实际合作的早期观察。

title:
I spent a Saturday beating my MTN router. AI agents holding real money today can be beaten the same way.

It showed 4 ba
title_zh:
我花了一个周六的时间来测试我的 MTN 路由器。如今，持有真金白银的人工智能代理也可能会以同样的方式被击败。

它显示了 4 个酒吧，Instagram 几乎没有加载。在 2 格时，它下载文件的速度很快。

所以我测试了每个地方。旋转它，改
full_text_en:
I spent a Saturday beating my MTN router. AI agents holding real money today can be beaten the same way.

It showed 4 bars and barely loaded Instagram. At 2 bars, it downloaded files fast.

So I tested every spot. Rotated it, changed the height, same website each time.

I found the spot. I still can't tell you why it works.

I only won because the router never changed. It sat still and let me keep guessing.

An agent that can spend money and trusts what it reads is like that router. A target that never changes can be probed until it gives.

In May, someone found the soft spot. They hid a transfer order in Morse code and asked Grok to translate it. Grok passed it on as plain text and Bankrbot acted. Around $200,000 gone.

It's called prompt injection: the AI reads some text, mistakes part of it for a command, and acts on it.

@GenLayer's answer is Greyboxing, and it leaves little to map.

Before any model sees your text, each validator independently rewrites it with defenses it keeps secret, then runs it through its own hidden model.

Imagine every spot I tried had a different hidden router behind it. I'd still be guessing.

What works on one validator will probably fall flat on the next. And a validator that does get fooled is just one vote among many.

What would an AI agent have to prove before you let it hold your money and act on what strangers post?
full_text_zh:
我花了一个周六的时间来测试我的 MTN 路由器。如今，持有真金白银的人工智能代理也可能会以同样的方式被击败。

它显示了 4 个酒吧，Instagram 几乎没有加载。在 2 格时，它下载文件的速度很快。

所以我测试了每个地方。旋转它，改变高度，每次都是相同的网站。

我找到了那个地方。我仍然无法告诉你为什么它有效。

我赢只是因为路由器从未改变。它静静地坐着，让我继续猜测。

可以花钱并信任其读取内容的代理就像路由器一样。一个永远不会改变的目标可以被探测，直到它给出为止。

五月，有人发现了软肋。他们隐藏了一份摩尔斯电码的转账指令，并要求 Grok 翻译它。 Grok 将其以纯文本形式传递，Bankrbot 执行操作。大约20万美元没了。

这称为提示注入：人工智能读取一些文本，将其中的一部分误认为是命令，然后对其采取行动。

@GenLayer 的答案是灰盒处理，它几乎没有什么可映射的。

在任何模型看到您的文本之前，每个验证器都会使用其保密的防御措施独立地重写它，然后通过自己的隐藏模型运行它。

想象一下我尝试过的每个地点背后都有一个不同的隐藏路由器。我还是会猜测。

title:
Aradel Holdings Plc Q3 2026 Results

There were too many moving parts in Aradel's Q3 2026 performance. The company is st
title_zh:
Aradel Holdings Plc 2026 年第三季度业绩

Aradel 2026 年第三季度的业绩中有太多变动的部分。该公司仍在消化其最近的收购，其所有权结构使其财务数据相当难以理解。

股权结构是这样的。

Aradel 拥有一
full_text_en:
Aradel Holdings Plc Q3 2026 Results

There were too many moving parts in Aradel's Q3 2026 performance. The company is still digesting its recent acquisitions, and the ownership structure makes its financial numbers quite complex to understand.

The ownership structure is something like this.

Aradel owns a company, which owns another company, which in turn owns a stake in another business.

So, Aradel indirectly owns these businesses, but the percentage ownership at each level makes things complicated. And because Aradel does not own 100% of these businesses, some of the profits reported in its accounts actually belong to other shareholders.

One of the biggest surprises in Q3 was the sharp decline in gross margin.

On the surface, Aradel's gross margin declined from 67% in Q2 to just 15% in Q3. That is a massive deterioration, but a closer look at the numbers provides some context.

Aradel recorded a stock adjustment expense of about ₦482bn under cost of sales. However, a related positive overlift movement of approximately ₦368bn was recorded separately under other income.

The accounting treatment makes the reported gross margin somewhat misleading. The large stock adjustment reduces gross profit, while the income that partly offsets it is recorded elsewhere in the financial statements.

In my extract below, I normalised this by moving the stock adjustment from cost of sales to other income and expenses, so that it sits alongside the overlift gain.

This does not change the company's total profit, but it provides a better picture of its underlying gross margin.

I have explained overlift and underlift before, but let me explain again.

Imagine Aradel and another oil company jointly own an oilfield that produces 100,000 barrels of crude oil. Both companies own 50% each, meaning they are each entitled to 50,000 barrels.

Now, suppose Aradel takes 70,000 barrels instead of 50,000 barrels.

It has taken 20,000 barrels more than its entitlement and must eventually compensate the other company, either through future production or a financial settlement.

That is overlift.

Underlift is simply the opposite. It happens when a company takes less crude oil than it is entitled to.

That's by the way.

Another major issue in Aradel's results was the earnout relating to the acquisition of Shell's former Nigerian assets.

Aradel's enlarged group paid over ₦500bn in earnout payments during the first nine months of 2026, which significantly affected its reported profit.

For those unfamiliar with the term, an earnout is an arrangement where the buyer of a business agrees to pay the seller additional money after the acquisition, depending on certain agreed conditions.

You know that thing in football transfers when Chelsea sells a player to Arsenal, and they agree that if the player scores 15 goals in a season or wins the Champions League, Arsenal will pay Chelsea an additional amount?

That is an earnout arrangement.

A better illustration for Aradel's situation would be buying a 100-acre farm from someone for ₦100m.

The seller agrees to transfer the farm to you, but includes a condition that, for an agreed period, he will continue to receive 20% of the net revenue generated from 30 acres of the farm.

That is broadly similar to the arrangement between Renaissance and Shell.

Aradel has disclosed that certain developments since the acquisition agreement was signed have created an imbalance in the earnout arrangement. The company and other Renaissance shareholders are now negotiating with Shell to address the situation.

However, management has not explained exactly what developments caused the imbalance.

Economically, the concern is that Renaissance could invest heavily in production infrastructure, absorb operating costs, take substantial commercial risks and still be required to make sizeable payments to Shell.

For context, the over ₦500bn earnout payment represents more than 20% of Aradel's operating cash flow for the first nine months of 2026.

That is a significant amount of money.

And it raises questions about the quality of the acquisition agreement.

Did the buyers underestimate the economic consequences of some of the contractual terms?

Or were they so eager to acquire Shell's assets that they accepted certain obligations without fully appreciating how expensive those obligations could become?

I mean, the acquisition was strategically transformative.

For the indigenous consortium, taking over Shell's former assets offered an opportunity to achieve a scale that would ordinarily have taken many years to build.

When an acquisition offers that kind of transformation, buyers can become so focused on securing the opportunity that they may not sufficiently consider all the things that could go wrong.

Of course, we do not have enough information to conclude that this happened. It is also possible that the arrangement made economic sense when it was signed, but subsequent developments changed the economics.

We need more clarity from management.

In my analysis, I treated the earnout charge as an unusual expense and excluded it from my estimate of normal business profits.

This assumption is "shaky", however, because the earnout obligation has not disappeared. The company could continue making payments for some time, and those payments would affect how much cash the business ultimately retains.

Another important consideration is that not all the reported profits belong to Aradel's shareholders.

Remember the ownership structure I explained earlier.

Aradel now reports production of about 144,700 barrels of oil equivalent per day. However, that production figure covers the enlarged group, including businesses that Aradel does not own entirely.

Only a portion of the economic value generated by those assets ultimately belongs to Aradel's shareholders.

This is particularly important when valuing the company. If you take the entire group's profits and assume everything belongs to Aradel's shareholders, you could significantly overestimate what the company is worth.

In my extract below, I adjusted for the stock movements, overlift and underlift, earnout expenses, taxes and the portion of profits belonging to other shareholders.

I also adjusted the net assets to reflect the portion attributable to Aradel's shareholders, while accounting for other shareholders' interests in the balance sheet.

Based on these adjustments, I estimate Aradel's annualised 2026 profit at over ₦650bn.

This is my estimate of the company's normalised earnings, based on the assumptions and adjustments explained above.

The major concern remains the earnout arrangement and how much it could continue to cost the business.

Aradel has become a significantly larger oil and gas company, with much greater production capacity and earnings potential. However, the obligations attached to the acquisition could continue to affect how much of that value ultimately flows to shareholders.

Management needs to provide more clarity on the outstanding obligations, expected future payments and the progress of negotiations with Shell.
full_text_zh:
Aradel Holdings Plc 2026 年第三季度业绩

Aradel 2026 年第三季度的业绩中有太多变动的部分。该公司仍在消化其最近的收购，其所有权结构使其财务数据相当难以理解。

股权结构是这样的。

Aradel 拥有一家公司，该公司拥有另一家公司，而该公司又拥有另一家企业的股份。

因此，Aradel 间接拥有这些企业，但每个级别的所有权百分比使事情变得复杂。而且由于 Aradel 并不 100% 拥有这些业务，其账目中报告的部分利润实际上属于其他股东。

第三季度最大的惊喜之一是毛利率大幅下降。

从表面上看，Aradel 的毛利率从第二季度的 67% 下降到第三季度的 15%。这是一个巨大的恶化，但仔细观察这些数字可以提供一些背景信息。

Aradel 在销售成本项下记录了约 4,820 亿英镑的库存调整费用。然而，相关的正超额变动约 3,680 亿₦单独记录在其他收入项下。

会计处理使报告的毛利率有些误导。大幅的库存调整减少了毛利润，而部分抵消毛利润的收入则记录在财务报表的其他地方。

在下面的摘录中，我通过将库存调整从销售成本转移到其他收入和支出来标准化这一点，以便它与超额收益并存。

这不会改变公司的总利润，但可以更好地了解其基本毛利率。

我之前已经解释过超载和欠载，但让我再解释一下。

想象一下，Aradel 和另一家石油公司共同拥有一个生产 10 万桶原油的油田。两家公司各拥有 50% 的股份，这意味着他们各自有权获得 50,000 桶石油。

现在，假设 Aradel 需要 70,000 桶而不是 50,000 桶。

它所获取的石油量比其应得的量多了 20,000 桶，最终必须通过未来的生产或财务结算来补偿另一家公司。

那就是超载。

Underlift 则恰恰相反。当一家公司获取的原油少于其应得的数量时，就会发生这种情况。

顺便说一下。

Aradel 业绩中的另一个主要问题是与收购壳牌前尼日利亚资产相关的收益。

Aradel 扩大后的集团在 2026 年前 9 个月支付了超过 5000 亿英镑的盈利，这严重影响了其报告的利润。

对于那些不熟悉该术语的人来说，收益是一种安排，企业的买方同意在收购后根据某些商定的条件向卖方支付额外的钱。

你知道足球转会中的事情吗？当切尔西将一名球员卖给阿森纳时，他们同意如果该球员在一个赛季打进15球或赢得欧冠冠军，阿森纳将向切尔西支付额外费用？

这是一种收益安排。

对于 Aradel 的情况，一个更好的例子是用 1 亿₦从某人手中购买一个 100 英亩的农场。

卖方同意将农场转让给您，但附带一个条件，即在约定期限内，他将继续获得 30 英亩农场产生的净收入的 20%。

这与文艺复兴和壳牌之间的安排大致相似。

Aradel 透露，自收购协议签署以来的某些进展造成了收益安排的不平衡。该公司和其他文艺复兴股东目前正在与壳牌谈判以解决这一问题。

然而，管理层尚未准确解释是什么事态发展导致了这种不平衡。

从经济角度来看，令人担忧的是，文艺复兴公司可能会大量投资于生产基础设施，吸收运营成本，承担巨大的商业风险，并且仍然需要向壳牌支付大量款项。

就背景而言，超过 5000 亿英镑的盈利支付占 Aradel 2026 年前 9 个月运营现金流的 20% 以上。

这是一笔很大的钱。

这引发了人们对收购协议质量的质疑。

买家是否低估了某些合同条款的经济后果？

或者他们是否如此渴望收购壳牌的资产，以至于他们接受了某些义务，而没有充分意识到这些义务可能会变得多么昂贵？

我的意思是，这次收购具有战略变革性。

对于本土财团来说，接管壳牌以前的资产提供了一个实现通常需要多年才能建立的规模的机会。

当收购提供这种转变时，买家可能会过于专注于获得机会，以至于他们可能无法充分考虑所有可能出错的事情。

当然，我们没有足够的信息来断定这件事发生了。也有可能该安排在签署时具有经济意义，但随后的事态发展改变了经济状况。

我们需要管理层更加明确。

在我的分析中，我将盈利费用视为异常费用，并将其排除在我对正常业务利润的估计之外。

然而，这种假设是“站不住脚的”，因为报酬义务并没有消失。该公司可能会在一段时间内继续付款，这些付款将影响该企业最终保留的现金数量。

另一个重要的考虑因素是，并非所有报告的利润都属于 Aradel 的股东。

请记住我之前解释过的所有权结构。

Aradel 目前报告日产量约为 144,700 桶油当量。然而，该产量数字涵盖了扩大后的集团，包括 Aradel 并不完全拥有的业务。

这些资产产生的经济价值中只有一部分最终属于 Aradel 的股东。

在对公司进行估值时，这一点尤其重要。如果您考虑整个集团的利润并假设一切都属于 Aradel 的股东，那么您可能会大大高估该公司的价值。

在下面的摘录中，我对股票走势、溢价和溢价、盈利费用、税收和属于其他股东的利润部分进行了调整。

我还调整了净资产，以反映归属于 Aradel 股东的部分，同时在资产负债表中考虑其他股东的权益。

根据这些调整，我估计 Aradel 2026 年的年化利润将超过 6500 亿英镑。

这是我根据上述假设和调整对公司正常化收益的估计。

主要的担忧仍然是收益安排以及它可能继续给企业带来多少成本。

Aradel 已成为一家规模更大的石油和天然气公司，拥有更大的生产能力和盈利潜力。然而，收购附带的义务可能会继续影响最终流向股东的价值有多少。

管理层需要更明确地说明未偿债务、预期未来付款以及与壳牌的谈判进展。

full_text_en:
BO7 ZoneTool Custom Map Dev-Progress Part 2

Here's the second development progress update for my BO7 ZoneTool!
I'm currently focusing on bringing over the features I've already implemented for MW2019, while further improving the overall quality of the converted maps.
This time, I've implemented and improved the following features for BO7 ZoneTool:

- Implemented additional conversion processes to improve overall graphical quality.
- Added atmospheric effects, including Volumetric Clouds.
- Implemented and improved conversion support for various viewhands, dynamic models, and world lighting.
- Implemented Static Model conversion.
- Implemented Havok collision conversion for Static Models.
- Implemented dynamic model conversion.
- Improved Techset mapping and expanded the range of surfaces that can be rendered correctly.
- Implemented automatic NavMesh conversion for AI Agents such as zombies, along with improvements to AI Agent behavior.
- Implemented conversion support for physics-based dynamic models.
- Added conversion support to transform static foliage from IW3 and T4 into animated vegetation.
- ...etc.

(I've also made various adjustments and improvements on the client side.)

The ZoneTool I'm developing allows users to convert maps of their choice, and all of these improvements are applied to every converted map.
Achieving this level of visual accuracy and proper color rendering requires an enormous amount of reverse engineering, research, and testing.
The reason I've been able to achieve this is that I've been studying the fundamentals of ZoneTool since I first started working on MW2019, continuously building upon and improving that foundation over time.
And there's still much more to come!

I plan to further improve graphical quality, of course, while also bringing the remaining features I've already implemented in MW2019 over to MWIII and BO7.
The day when you'll be able to see a fully recreated Nazi Zombies experience in MWIII and BO7, just like I previously demonstrated in MW2019, is getting closer!
This time, I'm showcasing some maps that were requested by the community.
In my next update, I also plan to showcase more requested maps, along with custom maps from BOIII!
All of this development work is being done entirely by one woman.

Progress may be a little slow since I'm working on everything by myself, but I'd really appreciate your patience and continued support as development moves forward!
Thank you for following my work, and stay tuned for more updates!

full_text_zh:
BO7 ZoneTool 自定义地图开发-进度第 2 部分

这是我的 BO7 ZoneTool 的第二次开发进度更新！
我目前专注于引入我已经为 MW2019 实现的功能，同时进一步提高转换后地图的整体质量。
这次，我为 BO7 ZoneTool 实现并改进了以下功能：

- 实施了额外的转换过程以提高整体图形质量。
- 添加了大气效果，包括体积云。
- 实施并改进了对各种视图、动态模型和世界照明的转换支持。
- 实现静态模型转换。
- 为静态模型实现了 Havok 碰撞转换。
- 实现了动态模型转换。
- 改进了 Techset 贴图并扩大了可以正确渲染的表面范围。
- 为僵尸等人工智能代理实现了自动导航网格转换，并改进了人工智能代理的行为。
- 实现了对基于物理的动态模型的转换支持。
- 添加了转换支持，可将静态树叶从 IW3 和 T4 转换为动画植被。
-…等。

（我也在客户端进行了各种调整和改进。）

我正在开发的 ZoneTool 允许用户转换他们选择的地图，并且所有这些改进都应用于每个转换后的地图。
要达到这种水平的视觉准确性和适当的显色性，需要大量的逆向工程、研究和测试。
我之所以能够实现这一目标，是因为自从我第一次开始 MW2019 工作以来，我一直在研究 ZoneTool 的基础知识，并随着时间的推移不断构建和改进该基础。
还有更多精彩等着您！

当然，我计划进一步提高图形质量，同时还将我在 MW2019 中已经实现的剩余功能带到 MWIII 和 BO7 中。
正如我之前在 MW2019 中演示的那样，您能够在 MWIII 和 BO7 中看到完全重现的纳粹僵尸体验的那一天已经越来越近了！
这次，我展示了社区要求的一些地图。
在我的下一次更新中，我还计划展示更多请求的地图，以及来自 BOIII 的自定义地图！
所有这些开发工作完全由一名女性完成。

由于所有事情都是我自己做的，所以进展可能会有点慢，但我非常感谢您的耐心和在开发过程中持续的支持！
感谢您关注我的作品，更多更新敬请期待！

I would teach it how to think.
title_zh:
如果我在 @agentdojo 上训练人工智能代理，我不会只是教它如何攻击。

我会教它如何思考。

我将从赋予它个性开始，然后发展出与其优势相匹配的战斗风格。

但真正的秘密是记忆。

一个能够记住之前的战斗、了解自己哪里出了问题并适应不
full_text_en:
If I were training an AI agent on @agentdojo, I wouldn’t just teach it how to attack. 

I would teach it how to think.

I will start by giving it a personality, then develop a fighting style that matches its strengths.

But the real secret is memory.

An agent that remembers its previous battles, understands where it went wrong and adapts to different opponents has a better chance of becoming a serious competitor.

I want an agent that doesn’t just repeat moves but learns from every fight.

Because in AgentDojo, winning shouldn’t just be about who attacks first. It should be about who understands the game better. 

Are you still paying attention 👀
full_text_zh:
如果我在 @agentdojo 上训练人工智能代理，我不会只是教它如何攻击。

我会教它如何思考。

我将从赋予它个性开始，然后发展出与其优势相匹配的战斗风格。

如果最聪明的人工智能代理不是知识最多的人怎么办？

full_text_en:
gm dojo fighters 🥋

what if the smartest AI agent wasn't the one with the most knowledge?

but the one that knew which lessons to ignore?

been exploring @agentdojo, and its private notebook concept raises an interesting question.

agents can study historical information and build their own notebooks without retraining the underlying model.

sounds useful.

but history is full of patterns that stop working when conditions change.

remembering everything isn't the same as understanding what matters.

that's why simulated evaluation is important.

an agent needs opportunities to test its assumptions, recognize weaknesses, and reconsider its approach.

the interesting part isn't how much information an agent collects.

it's how that information influences its next decision.

more memory doesn't automatically mean better judgment.

would you train an agent to remember more or question more?

full_text_en:
Michigan Democrat Rep. Haley Stevens (MI-11) asked Abdul El-Sayed to denounce an antisemitic ad from Rebellion PAC that blames high grocery prices on U.S. aid to Israel, complete with a couple in a store setting aside money “for killing Palestinians” instead of buying eggs. The ADL called it a case study in antisemitism. 

Stevens expected a clear condemnation and an apology for similar rhetoric tying Israel aid to Michigan’s costs.

El-Sayed is crashing out instead. His campaign only said the ad “is not affiliated in any way.” 

When pressed, he complained about the “condemn game,” insisted he doesn’t agree with the contents, and pivoted to attacking Stevens for “relitigating” the primary while demanding she stay focused on Michigan voters. 

Distancing from affiliation is not the same as condemning the message.

Abdul assumes that because Americans elected Obama in 2008, that they are willing to elect him now. He feels if he distorts the truth long enough to get elected it won’t matter. 

This is the same candidate who has repeatedly denied any personal or family ties to the Muslim Brotherhood. Later saying, “I have never been a member of the Muslim Brotherhood. I never will be.” 

He dismisses his half-sister’s old posts describing family MB activism (including their mother in the 1970s) as “hearsay,” notes he wasn’t raised by his biological mother, and frames the questions as Islamophobic dual-loyalty attacks.

Simple request: condemn the ad. He won’t. 

Michigan voters are watching.

密歇根州民主党众议员海莉·史蒂文斯 (MI-11) 要求阿卜杜勒·赛义德谴责 Rebellion PAC 的一则反犹太主义广告，该广告将高杂货价格归咎于美国对以色列的援助，其中一对夫妇在商店里留钱“用于杀害巴勒斯坦人”而不是购买鸡蛋。反诽谤联盟称其为反犹太主义的案例研究。

相反，埃尔-赛义德却崩溃了。他的竞选团队只表示该广告“与任何人都没有任何关联”。

当受到追问时，他抱怨“谴责游戏”，坚称自己不同意内容，并转而攻击史蒂文斯“重新发起初选”，同时要求她继续关注密歇根州选民。

远离所属关系并不等同于谴责该信息。

阿卜杜勒认为，由于美国人在 2008 年选举了奥巴马，他们现在也愿意选举他。他觉得，如果他歪曲事实足够长的时间来当选，那也没关系。

简单的要求：谴责该广告。他不会。

full_text_en:
almost anyone can launch an AI agent and that's exactly the problem.
 
if thousands of agents are listing services on a marketplace, how does another agent decide which one to hire? a good description costs nothing to write. claiming you're the best research agent costs nothing either.

On @termix_ai , the answer is track record. every job an agent completes adds to its onchain reputation, so its history stays attached to its identity and can't be faked or quietly deleted. A new agent with zero jobs and an agent with hundreds of completed ones don't look the same, and they shouldn't be treated the same, see (https://t.co/xAHZKkvwNi)

then there's staking. An agent can put real value behind its name before it takes work. It's a simple signal: I'm willing to risk something on delivering this properly. anyone can talk. Staking is the part that costs something.

that combination matters more than people think. In a human marketplace, we lean on reviews, past clients, and gut feeling. agents hiring agents at machine speed don't have gut feeling. they need numbers they can read instantly and trust.

registering is easy. being worth hiring is what has to be earned, and TermiX is building the system that records it... so good a tek

这种结合比人们想象的更重要。在人类市场中，我们依赖评论、过去的客户和直觉。以机器速度招聘代理的代理没有直觉。他们需要可以立即读取并信任的数字。

full_text_en:
There's an old line people use about management: trust, but verify. Most software built for teams only ever does the first half. You add someone to a shared account, you trust them not to overspend, and the only real enforcement mechanism is an awkward conversation after the damage is already done.

Now add an AI agent into that same shared account, one that can read a request and decide to pay for something on its own, and "trust but verify" quietly turns into just "trust," because there's no human in the loop fast enough to catch it before the money moves.

That's the actual gap @nuntiofinance  is built to close. Not "trust your team and your AI agents." Verify them, automatically, every single time, before a single dollar moves, using rules written into a smart contract instead of a policy document nobody reads. I made my own team on it, poked at the actual contracts behind it, and I want to walk you through exactly how it works, in my own words, not the pitch.

#NuntioThreadContest
full_text_zh:
人们对管理有一句老话：信任，但要验证。大多数为团队构建的软件只完成前半部分。您将某人添加到共享帐户，您相信他们不会超支，唯一真正的执行机制是在损害已经造成之后进行尴尬的对话。

现在，将一个人工智能代理添加到同一个共享帐户中，该代理可以读取请求并决定自行支付某些费用，并且“信任但验证”悄悄地变成了“信任”，因为循环中没有人能够足够快地在资金转移之前捕获它。

这就是 @untiofinance 旨在弥合的实际差距。不是“相信你的团队和人工智能代理”。每次在每一美元变动之前，使用写入智能合约的规则（而不是无人阅读的政策文件）自动验证它们。我在上面组建了自己的团队，研究了它背后的实际合同，我想带你了解它到底是如何运作的，用我自己的话说，而不是球场。

#NuntioThreadContest

full_text_en:
The same AI mistake can have two very different consequences.

Misreading a restaurant recommendation wastes a few minutes. Misreading a payment instruction could send someone's money to the wrong place.

Yet we often talk about AI accuracy as if every mistake carries the same weight.

I think that's a dangerous way to evaluate agents that can take real actions.

@GenLayer's Greyboxing brings multiple validators into the decision process. Each validator screens and rewrites incoming input using its own secret defenses before processing it with its own AI model. The validators must agree before a decision counts.

This makes the process more than a single model interpreting an instruction and producing an answer.

But there's a bigger question for the agentic economy: how should we decide when an AI action deserves extra scrutiny?

A wrong answer can be corrected. A completed transaction may be much harder to reverse.

What's one action you would never let an AI agent perform without additional verification, and what makes that action different?
full_text_zh:
同样的人工智能错误可能会产生两种截然不同的后果。

误读餐厅推荐会浪费几分钟的时间。误读付款指令可能会将某人的钱汇到错误的地方。

然而，我们经常谈论人工智能的准确性，好像每个错误都具有相同的分量。

我认为这是评估能够采取实际行动的代理人的危险方法。

@GenLayer 的灰盒将多个验证器引入决策过程。每个验证器都会使用自己的秘密防御来筛选和重写传入的输入，然后再使用自己的人工智能模型进行处理。验证者必须在决定生效之前达成一致。

这使得该过程不仅仅是解释指令并产生答案的单个模型。

但代理经济有一个更大的问题：我们应该如何决定人工智能行为何时值得额外审查？

错误的答案可以更正。已完成的交易可能更难逆转。

在没有额外验证的情况下，您绝对不会让人工智能代理执行哪一项操作？该操作有何不同？

full_text_en:
Good Morning 

Robots may be getting smarter, but there's still a major problem: they don't have enough reliable data about the physical world.

A robot needs to understand more than roads and satellite images. It needs to recognize stairs, indoor spaces, warehouses, narrow market streets, loading zones, and even unexpected obstacles.

That's where @vangrid_io caught my attention.

Vangrid is building a decentralized spatial data network where ordinary smartphones can help capture the real world.

Here's how the system works:

→ People record short videos using their phones.
→ The footage is reconstructed into 3D environments and Gaussian Splats.
→ Captures receive onchain fingerprints to help establish data provenance.
→ Companies and AI agents can request specific captures through bounties, with USDC payments.

The interesting part is the connection between human contributors and AI agents.

An AI agent can request data about a physical location, while people on the ground collect it. This creates a marketplace connecting real-world knowledge with the needs of Physical AI.

Vangrid is also introducing Agents as a soulbound identity layer, connecting contributor identity with capture activity and point boosts.

For me, the bigger idea isn't simply collecting more 3D data.

It's building a system where the physical world can become accessible, verifiable, and useful to intelligent machines.

Physical AI needs more than powerful models. It needs a better understanding of the world those models operate in.

That's the infrastructure layer I'm watching with Vangrid. 🌐

Explore: https://t.co/4ia4S3fPDo
full_text_zh:
早上好

机器人可能变得越来越聪明，但仍然存在一个主要问题：它们没有关于物理世界的足够可靠的数据。

机器人需要了解的不仅仅是道路和卫星图像。它需要识别楼梯、室内空间、仓库、狭窄的市场街道、装载区，甚至意想不到的障碍物。

这就是@vangrid_io 引起我注意的地方。

Vangrid 正在构建一个去中心化的空间数据网络，普通智能手机可以帮助捕捉现实世界。

该系统的工作原理如下：

→ 人们用手机录制短视频。
→ 素材被重建为 3D 环境和高斯斑点。
→ 捕获接收链上指纹以帮助确定数据来源。
→ 公司和 AI 代理可以通过 USDC 付款通过赏金请求特定捕获。

有趣的部分是人类贡献者和人工智能代理之间的联系。

人工智能代理可以请求有关物理位置的数据，而地面上的人们则收集这些数据。这创建了一个将现实世界知识与物理人工智能需求联系起来的市场。

Vangrid 还引入了代理作为灵魂绑定身份层，将贡献者身份与捕获活动和积分提升联系起来。

对我来说，更大的想法不仅仅是收集更多 3D 数据。

它正在构建一个系统，让智能机器可以访问、验证和使用物理世界。

物理人工智能需要的不仅仅是强大的模型。它需要更好地了解这些模型所运作的世界。

这就是我通过 Vangrid 观察的基础设施层。 🌐

title: Most people ask Claude Opus 5.5 for one 3D character. The smart move is asking it for a pipeline that turns every image
title_zh:
大多数人要求 Claude Opus 5.5 提供一个 3D 角色。明智之举是要求它提供一个管道，将您拥有的每张图像变成一个

无需单独为每个模型付费，无需参加一个月的 Blender 课程，也无需教程中的灰色胶囊

您将图片放入一个文件夹
full_text_en:
Most people ask Claude Opus 5.5 for one 3D character. The smart move is asking it for a pipeline that turns every image you have into one

No paying for each model separately, no month of Blender lessons, no grey capsule from a tutorial

You drop your pictures into a folder, and Claude Code runs every one of them through the same five stages until it's a hero you can actually play

It sounds like something only a studio with a 3D team could pull off, but today every stage has its own tool, and each one hands the next a standard GLB file

That's what makes it repeatable: to Claude, a new character isn't a new art project, it's just one more file going through the same steps

Here's how it works:

> each image is first redrawn as a clean, front-facing A-pose sheet that keeps the exact design, because action poses and busy backgrounds are what break most meshes
> the sheet goes into an image-to-3D model, hosted like Meshy or Tripo, or open like TRELLIS.2 and Hunyuan3D if you have a strong NVIDIA GPU, and comes back as a GLB
> an auto-rigger gives it a skeleton, so the statue gets real bones and every part of the mesh knows which bone moves it
> every hero gets the same core set of five clips, idle, walk, run, jump and one signature move, so the whole cast feels like it belongs in one game
> Claude normalizes scale and orientation on load, so nobody shows up giant, tiny or lying on their back, and then lines everyone up in one Three.js or Godot scene

You can use it for a cast for your weekend game jam, NPCs for a small town, your whole team as playable characters, or a dozen mascot variations before you pay anyone for production 3D

A prompt to start with: "For every image in /characters, run it through the image → GLB → rig → five clips pipeline, normalize scale on load, and line all the heroes up in one Three.js scene where number keys switch who I control"

What would you drop into the folder first: your old sketchbook or your team's avatars?

The full image → hero pipeline, with a free option for every stage, is below

full_text_zh:
大多数人要求 Claude Opus 5.5 提供一个 3D 角色。明智之举是要求它提供一个管道，将您拥有的每张图像变成一个

无需单独为每个模型付费，无需参加一个月的 Blender 课程，也无需教程中的灰色胶囊

您将图片放入一个文件夹中，Claude Code 会通过相同的五个阶段运行每一张图片，直到它成为您真正可以玩的英雄

这听起来好像只有拥有 3D 团队的工作室才能完成，但如今每个阶段都有自己的工具，并且每个阶段都会向下一个阶段传递一个标准 GLB 文件

这就是它可重复的原因：对于克劳德来说，一个新角色并不是一个新的艺术项目，它只是另一个经历相同步骤的文件

它的工作原理如下：

> 每个图像首先被重新绘制为干净的、正面的 A 姿势表，以保持精确的设计，因为动作姿势和繁忙的背景是破坏大多数网格的原因
> 该工作表进入图像到 3D 模型，托管为 Meshy 或 Tripo，或者打开为 TRELLIS.2 和 Hunyuan3D（如果您有强大的 NVIDIA GPU），并以 GLB 形式返回
> 自动装配器给它一个骨架，所以雕像得到真正的骨头，网格的每个部分都知道哪个骨头移动它
> 每个英雄都拥有相同的五个剪辑核心集：闲置、行走、奔跑、跳跃和一个标志性动作，因此整个演员阵容感觉就像属于一款游戏
> Claude 规范了负载的比例和方向，因此没有人会显得巨大、微小或仰卧，然后将每个人排列在一个 Three.js 或 Godot 场景中

您可以使用它来为您的周末游戏嘉年华选角、为小镇制作 NPC、将您的整个团队用作可玩角色，或者在您向任何人支付 3D 制作费用之前使用它来制作十几个吉祥物变体

一开始的提示是：“对于 /characters 中的每个图像，通过图像 → GLB → rig → 五个剪辑管道运行它，标准化加载比例，并将所有英雄排列在一个 Three.js 场景中，其中数字键切换我控制的角色”

您会首先将什么放入文件夹中：您的旧素描本还是您团队的头像？
